mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the periods when FEDFUNDS has been declining for at least 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that may lead to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of the instances where UNRATE has been above 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential construction permits (HOUST) and a rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a contraction in housing demand and rising cost pressures, which together indicate an economic slowdown that reduces corporate profit growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the periods when HOUST declines and CPIAUCSL rises, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, it signals supply chain constraints that increase input costs and reduce corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the periods when INDPRO is below 100.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the past 6 months indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the periods when PAYEMS has been increasing for at least 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 1.5% and remains above that level for three consecutive months, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances where FEDFUNDS has been above 1.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) signals a monetary tightening combined with weakening demand, which together reduce corporate earnings growth and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the periods when FEDFUNDS is rising and RSAFS is declining, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL above 2.5%) and declining residential construction (HOUST below 700,000 units), demand-side pressures intensify, leading to higher interest rates and reduced consumer spending, which cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the periods when CPIAUCSL is above 2.5% and HOUST is below 700.
